name: TCPL Packaging Ltd
title: TCPL Packaging Ltd-$ - 523301 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Flexible packaging running well-utilised with a fourth line due by year-end, carton utilisation lower, FY27 capex ~INR 100 crore; paper cost increases still rolling through with no margin guidance, export recovery contingent on Middle East.

summary.headline: TCPL Packaging Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose over 9% YoY to INR 465 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.4% including forex-led other income.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income was INR 465 crore (over 9% YoY) and EBITDA including other income was INR 81 crore (17.4% margin), helped by operational export forex gains. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,836 crore (+3% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 318 crore (17.3%). Exports were hit in Q4 by Middle East disruptions, while domestic volumes grew ahead of consumer market trends. Management said margins were pressured by raw material inflation and a lag in passing on price hikes, and the company declined to give margin or export guidance beyond the near term. Finance cost rose on a INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on ECB, and deferred tax was higher due to capex-related timing differences.

segments.name: Flexible packaging
segments.commentary: Management called FY26 a strong year with healthy utilisation; the last commercialised line runs at optimum level. A fourth line at the unit is expected to be commercialised by year-end FY27, with management expecting its return on assets to beat lines 2 and 3.

segments.name: Folding cartons (consumer products, mainly FMCG and F&B)
segments.commentary: Management said this is more than half of the business. Carton utilisation is lower, with some double-digit scope for growth in existing capacity.

segments.name: Paperboard (Chennai greenfield)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is above 50% and rising on new customer approvals; management expects a good ramp-up ahead.

segments.name: Creative (Noida)
segments.commentary: Management said it just squeaked through to EBITDA break-even in FY25 and improved further in FY26, with a target of cash and net profit in FY27. Electronics demand weakness is a headwind.

segments.name: Recyclable films
segments.commentary: Domestic uptake is weak because EPR rules mandate recycled content, not recyclable packaging. Output is rising through export jobs, and machinery issues are resolved.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management expects margins to hold if raw material cost increases stop, and said a prolonged crisis would make further price pass-through difficult.

FY27 capex is guided at about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, with the bulk in flexible packaging and some building expansion; management said the plan is calibrated and could rise if demand picks up.
Exports expected to recover in FY27 if Middle East conditions normalise; management is optimistic about the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Domestic demand expected to be good for the year, but fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit consumer demand in coming quarters.
Utilisation at the Chennai and cylinder facilities is expected to improve over the next one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, mainly flexible packaging with some factory building expansion.
Fourth flexible packaging line at the unit expected to be commercialised by end FY27, with a temporary absorption-period drag on profitability.
Chennai greenfield paperboard facility above 50% utilised and ramping up on customer approvals.
Gravure cylinder facility at Silvassa commissioned recently and ramped up well, adding backward integration.
Management said capex intensity may rise as new initiatives materialise; the current plan is considered firm.
demand_pricing: Domestic volume growth ahead of underlying consumer market trends; management said momentum is okay with no demand problem currently, and it is broad-based across customers.
Exports were under pressure in Q4 due to Middle East disruptions; some vessels are sailing again after the ceasefire, but the outlook is highly uncertain.
Paper and board prices kept rising; virgin board increased sharply, and recycled board sees steady incremental increases that are harder to pass through.
Company adds more than one or two customers almost every month and is expanding its export team.
Electronics volumes are falling due to chip price increases; diversification into other packaging areas is offsetting this.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and which regions could scale beyond the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly optimistic on export recovery if the Middle East normalises, citing scaling in the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia. It gave no quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost high despite debt levels, and is the ECB unhedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on the ECB raised interest cost. It is a notional, non-cash accounting item. Absolute debt grew on a standalone basis and fell marginally on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is deferred tax so high this year and is it linked to capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the actual tax outgo is already reflected, and the higher deferred tax is a timing difference from capex-driven tax vs accounting depreciation. It said the annual tax rate is in line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a domestic/export revenue split annually?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider providing the split, possibly offline, but did not commit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pickup in recyclable film demand, and how is Creative progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic recyclable film demand is weak until the government mandates recyclable packaging. Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management aims for cash and net profit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and is there a plan to expand into new sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, and calibrated given uncertainty. Management said it adds one or two customers almost every month across sectors and is not sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 margins be higher with Chennai and cylinder ramp-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty. It said margins should improve with better utilisation if conditions are better.

qa_highlights.question: Is paper cost still rising, and what is the impact of the minimum import price on board?
qa_highlights.answer: Paper cost pressure continues, with virgin board up sharply and recycled board rising steadily. The MIP on board imports gives domestic mills some room, and management expects some price increase is inevitable.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and shipping disruption could keep export volumes weak and extend raw material inflation.
Continuing steady paper and board price increases could limit pass-through and compress margins.
ECB mark-to-market exposure to euro movements could keep adding to finance cost.
Deferred tax charges from capex timing differences could continue to weigh on reported PAT and EPS.
Monitor utilisation at Chennai, the cylinder facility and the fourth flexible line, plus the Creative break-even trajectory.
Fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit domestic consumer demand in coming quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand and long-term export growth, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, exports and FY28 outlook, citing the Middle East crisis and cost volatility. Management tended to defer specifics on guidance and deflected the finance cost and tax questions to accounting timing.
key_quotes: So, we do expect to have a good year for domestic as well.
I cannot tell you what is going to happen in 3 months. So, I am not going to speculate about 1.5 years down the line where anything can happen, as we have seen.
Just annualize it and see, do not go quarter-by-quarter, I think. Overall, it is fine.
But we add like more than one or two customers almost every month. So, that is a constant process.

adds.what: Fourth flexible packaging line at the unit
Chennai greenfield paperboard facility (above 50% utilised and ramping up)
Gravure cylinder facility at Silvassa (backward integration)

growth.why: No formal revenue or margin guidance; management declined beyond near term, citing Middle East export drag and raw material inflation, with FY27 capex of about INR 100 crore and a fourth flexible packaging line expected by end FY27 as the main capacity support.
